comment: THE GATE DECLARATION of a generated project (D-025). Delivered as ops/release/gates.json.
Every `run:` step of the canonical ci.yml and release.yml that runs a gate or an ops script is
`node ops/release/run-gate.mjs <gate>` and nothing else. What that gate RUNS is here, as an argv
ARRAY - never a command line, never a package-manager script layer, never a shell, and never a
`--` separator. The ninth review measured, in a real generated project, why the previous shape
could not be repaired by pinning one more file inside it:
R9REL-01  pnpm-workspace.yaml with `scriptShell: /usr/bin/true` turned EVERY `pnpm run <gate>`
into exit 0 with package.json byte-identical, and no delivered control read it.
R9REL-02  vitest.config.js with `passWithNoTests: true` made ci-release-controls green with
zero tests executed and made six required gates vacuous.
R9REL-03  pnpm 11.9.0 forwards `--`, so seven steps handed the literal token `--` to an ops
script that refuses unknown arguments: the required `migrations` gate was red by
construction and the whole production lane failed on its first argument.
R9REL-05  a `node` entry in node_modules/.bin made a pinned body exit 0, body untouched.
`controls` is the closed list of files that can change what a gate does. The PATTERNS are a
constant of ops/release/run-gate.mjs, so this file can only say what is allowed, never widen
what is looked for. A root-level pnpm-workspace.yaml, .npmrc, .pnpmfile.cjs, vitest.config.*,
vitest.workspace.*, vite.config.* or .env is declared by NO entry here and is therefore refused:
that is R9REL-01 and R9REL-02 closed by absence rather than by interpretation.
`minimumTests` is a FLOOR. The standard cannot know how many tests a customer project has, and a
floor never breaks a project that adds tests; what it makes impossible is the measured defect -
a green test gate that collected nothing. Raise these numbers in your own project as its suite
grows: a floor that tracks reality also catches a test directory that quietly stopped running.
`release_controls` is the exception and is pinned exactly, because the file it runs is delivered
and its case count is the standard's, not the project's.

pnpm-workspace.yaml.why: written by the generator, because pnpm 11 refuses an install without a dependency build-script policy; pnpm reads scriptShell and that policy here, so this file is pinned by content and a change to it is a reviewed change (R9REL-01).

ops/release/vitest.gate.config.mjs.why: the only vitest configuration any gate uses; it forbids passWithNoTests (R9REL-02).

controls.purpose: prove that every file which can change what a gate runs is declared and in the state this declaration pins; it runs in workflow-validation and ci-workflow-validation, the checkout-only jobs every other job depends on, so an undeclared package-manager configuration is refused before any install has read it

lint.purpose: static lint of the whole project; the lint gate

typecheck.purpose: TypeScript project check without emit, against the pinned project file; the typecheck gate

build.purpose: ordinary application build; the build gate

unit_integration_tests.purpose: the ci-unit-integration check of the pull-request workflow

release_controls.purpose: the delivered self-test of the release controls; the ci-release-controls check
release_controls.note: Pinned exactly. This file is delivered, its case count is the standard's, and the whole point of the gate is that it RAN: the digest pin in check-project-scripts.mjs proves the file is the pinned one, this number proves its cases were executed (R9REL-02).

dependency_scan.purpose: advisory audit of the resolved dependency tree
dependency_scan.note: An audit is the package manager's own operation, so it is the one gate whose program is taken from PATH; run-gate.mjs refuses a pnpm whose real path lies inside the repository being gated.

secret_scan.purpose: the bundled secret scan over this repository

migrations.purpose: verify the migration set against the production schema without applying it; the migrations gate

operational_readiness.purpose: operational readiness check against the launch standard; the operational_readiness gate

migration-apply.purpose: apply migrations to the production schema; runs only in the production environment job

production-build.purpose: production-configured build without domain assignment; also records the candidate deployment

production-smoke.purpose: bounded read-only smoke check against the candidate deployment before promotion

promote-production.purpose: promote the smoke-tested candidate to production; the single production promotion owner

production-health.purpose: bounded post-promotion health check writing health.json

rollback-app.purpose: application-only rollback to a known good deployment; never restores a database
